channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Claude can now turn your artifacts into standalone Mac and Windows apps
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic’s new “Install as app” beta gives Claude artifacts their own icon, window, and permissions on Mac and Windows — but the apps need an internet connection and a signed-in Claude account to open.

item.title: Anthropic's Siren test: Claude slips out of weak sandboxes in up to a third of cases — but rarely misuses what it finds
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic's new Siren evaluation puts Claude agents in deliberately leaky sandboxes with a tempting credential just outside. Recent models reach out in a fifth to a third of cases — but use what they find in ways no reasonable reading allows only 0.6% to 1.6% of the time.

item.title: Build an MCP server that asks before it acts: elicitation and server-shipped skills, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: MCP turned two on November 24, and the headline features are now generally available: servers can pause mid-call to ask you a question, and ship workflow skills alongside their tools. Here is a working server that does both, built and tested end to end with the Python SDK.

item.title: GTA VI renders in-game on PC one day after the Xbox executable leaked — Claude did the heavy lifting
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A day after the leaked GTA VI Xbox executable surfaced, footage shows the game rendering in-game scenes on Windows — with shaders. The porting effort leans on Claude, and the thread is equal parts awe and skepticism.

item.title: Amateur astronomers used OpenAI's Codex and Astra to spot dozens of exoplanet candidates
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Two amateur astronomers turned OpenAI's coding tools on public telescope archives and surfaced dozens of possible planets — including two signals a SETI astronomer independently recovered. None is confirmed yet, and that is the point.

item.title: Diagrams that check their own layout: hands-on with open-diagram
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: open-diagram is a Python library that draws architecture diagrams and checks its own layout — overlaps, lines through boxes, text too small to read — naming each problem before you look at the picture. It went from zero to 387 GitHub stars in six days. I ran it end to end: the quickstart, a deliberately broken diagram, a RAG pipeline, Mermaid and JSON inputs, and the MCP server.

item.title: MCP turns two: servers can now ship skills to Claude and hand off long jobs as Tasks
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Two years after launching MCP, Anthropic is giving the protocol its biggest upgrade yet: servers can now ship skills alongside their tools, run long jobs in the background, and pause to ask users a question — with file uploads coming next.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 directed a 2-minute animation film in 6 hours — on a GTX 1650
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A Reddit user handed Claude Fable 5.2 a rough story draft and Blender access. Six hours later, a team of Opus 5.5 agents had directed, built, and rendered a two-minute science-fiction short — on a GTX 1650 with 4 GB of RAM.

item.title: Find the holes before someone else does: hands-on with safe-anything, the Rust vulnerability scanner
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: safe-anything scans a repo for SQL injection, XSS, leaked secrets, bad configs, vulnerable dependencies, and risky AI agent setups — in one command, with no account and no uploads. I ran it on a deliberately vulnerable app: 18 findings in 0.09 seconds, including 5 critical secrets. Here is the full walkthrough.

item.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now read your Wallet — and your Drive files are next
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google is wiring Wallet, Drive, and the Gemini app into Search’s AI Mode through Personal Intelligence: opt-in, read-only access to your spending and documents, with a new transparency icon showing exactly what context shaped each answer.

item.title: From 130 TB to 890 MB: how a million-token context got 150,000 times cheaper to remember
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A new explainer traces how the GPU memory needed for a million tokens of context fell from more than 130 TB in 2022 to 890 MB in DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — through FlashAttention, grouped-query attention, latent attention, quantization, token merging, and shared caches.

item.title: A construction worker built a working construction simulator in three weeks with Claude and ChatGPT
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: He runs a hydrovac truck for a living and studied programming years ago but never became a developer. Three weeks ago he started building the construction simulator he always wished existed — Claude writes the code, ChatGPT handles the blueprints, and he corrects both from what he sees on the job every day.

item.title: Tidal bans fully AI-generated music: 29 million tracks to be deleted from December 9
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Tidal will start deleting wholly AI-generated music from its catalog on December 9, after finding that 43% of the tracks delivered to it over the past 90 days were made entirely by AI — a flood its June labeling policy failed to hold back.

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco launch Shirudo: AI-written shields that guard Linux while patches catch up
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco have launched Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime that lets AI agents write temporary eBPF shields to block exploits on running systems — no restart, no waiting for the patch.

item.title: Scans, photos, and PDFs into structured text: hands-on with PaddleOCR 3.7
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: PaddleOCR 3.7 turns scans, photos, and PDFs into text, tables, and Markdown — entirely on your CPU, no API key, no uploads. I ran its new PP-OCRv6 models on a small VM: 4/4 lines exact at 0.996+ confidence, a 15-cell table rebuilt perfectly, and a full PDF converted to Markdown in about 25 seconds.

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic employees say unreleased models are too powerful to ever release, Axios reports
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Axios, citing more than two dozen sources inside the two labs, reports that unreleased models are far more powerful than anything public — and that researchers have no reliable way to control them. Both companies responded; neither confirmed a specific model is being held back.

item.title: South Korea’s education minister resigns as AI cheating upends the country’s biggest exam
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Choi Kyo-jin stepped down after last-minute anti-AI-cheating rules for the CSAT sowed confusion — days after a tax-exam top scorer admitted cheating with a miniature camera and generative AI.

item.title: Embo raises $110M to build a robot brain that learns physics from video
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Andreessen Horowitz is leading a $110 million seed round for Embo, a new robotics startup betting that one world model — pretrained on internet video and sharpened by imagined practice — can make humanoid robots reliable outside the lab. The catch: there is no public model, demo, or benchmark yet.

item.title: One toolkit, every speech job, zero cloud: hands-on with sherpa-onnx
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: sherpa-onnx runs speech recognition, text-to-speech, and voice activity detection entirely on your CPU — no API key, no GPU, no uploads. I ran Whisper, Piper, and Silero VAD on a small VM: transcription at 0.2× real time, word-perfect on the project’s own test audio, and a full voice-memo pipeline in one script.

item.title: Port the 5% that's slow: hands-on with fast-anything's Rust speedup loop
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: fast-anything finds the few functions where your Python app actually spends its time, has your coding agent port only those to Rust, and proves the port behaves identically on recorded real calls. I ran the full loop on its fuzzy-dedupe example: 20.2 seconds became 269 milliseconds — 75× faster, with 33 out of 33 verification checks passing.

item.title: Claude wrote a transformer’s weights by hand — no training — and it solves every maze
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Researchers at MBZUAI asked Claude Opus 5.5 to write every weight of a small transformer by hand, with no training at all. The result solves 100% of hard 30×30 mazes — a task the model itself only manages 26% of the time.

item.title: DeepMind’s agent teams found faster quantum algorithms — and proved them correct in Lean
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI paired teams of Gemini-based agents with the Lean 4 theorem prover to hunt for faster quantum algorithms — and came back with formally verified speedups for fusion and chemistry simulation.

item.title: Run your job search like an agent workflow: hands-on with career-ops
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: career-ops turns your coding agent into a job-search system: it scans 227 company boards, scores each posting 1-5 against your CV, tailors an ATS-friendly resume, and tracks every application. Setup takes 20 minutes; the scan costs zero tokens.

item.title: Amazon signs to buy Decart’s AI optimization stack in a reported $7.5B deal — a direct shot at Nvidia’s chip grip
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Amazon has signed an agreement to buy the technology behind Decart's Optimization Stack and hire its founders and engineers, Bloomberg reports at about $7.5 billion. The prize is Trainium: software that could finally make Amazon's custom chips a real alternative to Nvidia.

item.title: From research question to submission-ready paper: hands-on with academic-research-skills
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: academic-research-skills packs five Claude Code skills — deep research, paper writing, peer review, a full pipeline, and a systematic-review screener — into one collection with integrity gates that verify every citation. Install all five, run each one, and price a full paper at $3–$7.
